title: Python Lists and Mutation
description: Read and update lists with indexing, slicing, append, pop, and copy operations.

questions.explanation: append adds one item to the end of the existing list.

questions.prompt: What does list.pop() do when no index is provided?
options: Removes and returns the last item
Removes and returns the first item
Returns the last item without changing the list
Raises an error because an index is required
questions.correct: Removes and returns the last item
questions.explanation: pop without an index removes the final item and gives that item back to the caller.

questions.prompt: A list can contain values of different Python types.
questions.explanation: Python lists can hold mixed values, although a consistent type often makes a program easier to reason about.
Negative indexes count from the end, so -1 selects the last item, which is green here.

questions.prompt: Which expression makes a shallow copy of a list named values?
questions.explanation: copy returns a new list with the same top-level items; assignment alone creates another name for the same list.
The slice starts at index 1 and stops before index 3.

options: Adds it after the last item
questions.explanation: insert takes an index and places the new value before the item currently at that position.

questions.prompt: Calling append returns the changed list as its result.
questions.explanation: append changes the list and returns None. Inspect the list afterward to see the mutation.
Index 1 refers to the second item, so assignment replaces 2 with 9.

questions.prompt: Which value is the first item in ['a', 'b', 'c']?
questions.explanation: The first item is at index 0, and the value stored there is a.
